newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open unchanged to down 2.00.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open unchanged to down 2.00.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open Tuesday unchanged to 2.00 cents per lb lower on Tuesday, dealers said.
The market is expected to continue its ascent in the near term, however, with technical resistance in July pegged above Monday's highs at 220 and 224 cents. Support was noted at 187.40 cents.
Open interest on the May contract fell by 1,634 lots as of Friday's close to 5,044 lots. Traders said they expected Monday's activity to have erased another 1,000-2,000 lots.
Following Monday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 2,250 lots to 61,099 lots.

CSCE coffee ended slightly lower in volatile trading on Monday. Most-active July futures ended down 0.10 cent a lb at 194.05, having traded from 187.50 to a new contract high of 199. Spot May fell 1.65, to 214.90.
The day's volume was estimated at 10,839 lots.

News that Colombia's truck drivers had begun a strike sparked early buying which sent prices up to new life-of-contract highs. As of late Monday, talks aimed at ending the two-day strike ended with no agreement reached.

LIFFE coffee futures were slightly higher and rangebound on Tuesday amid light fund buying and trade selling overhead, dealers said. At the midsession break, May stood $5 higher at $1,648 and July up $7 at $1,676.
